market_name: Will 6 Fed rate cuts happen in 2026?

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Check whether the market probability move is corroborated by moves in 2y/10y Treasury yields and Fed funds futures (SOFR/SR3 strips); isolated prediction-market move with no rates follow-through is noise.
time_plan.1h: Confirm TLT direction aligns with yield move; watch for any Fed speak or data release that could be the underlying catalyst.
time_plan.2h: Assess persistence — is the dovish repricing holding or fading? Compare against DXY and equity index behavior for macro consistency.
time_plan.6h: Re-evaluate whether the move reflects genuine recession/easing fear vs. a soft-landing dovish mix; check gold and credit spreads for confirmation.
time_plan.12h: Mark cumulative TLT return vs. expectation; note whether the prediction-market shift preceded or lagged the public rates move.

predictions.reasoning: A sharp rise in the implied probability of 6 Fed cuts in 2026 reflects a dovish repricing of the policy path, consistent with lower expected front-end and long-end yields. Lower yields lift long-duration bond prices, making TLT the cleanest liquid proxy. A dovish surprise is usually driven by softer growth/inflation data or an easing bias, both bullish for duration.

trade_eligibility.reason: Below minimum expected move or unclear direction.

time_plan.30m: Verify DXY is weakening and real yields (TIPS) falling alongside the dovish repricing; if dollar is firm, gold thesis weakens.
time_plan.1h: Check gold vs. real-yield correlation holding; watch for competing safe-haven/risk-on flows.
time_plan.2h: Reassess whether dovishness is growth-scare driven (ambiguous for gold via risk flows) or pure rate-cut driven (clearly bullish).
time_plan.6h: Compare gold move magnitude to TLT; divergence suggests idiosyncratic metal flows rather than macro signal.
time_plan.12h: Mark GLD return vs. expectation and document relationship to the rate-cut probability shift.

predictions.reasoning: Expectations of six 2026 cuts imply lower real rates and a weaker dollar, both supportive of gold. Gold is a liquid, broad macro proxy for an aggressively dovish Fed path, though its response is noisier than rates because it also carries risk-sentiment and inflation components.

evidence_used: Market question tracks number of 25bp Fed cuts in 2026 — a direct read on expected monetary easing
Six cuts (150bp) is an aggressively dovish outcome implying recession risk or a sharp easing cycle
Standard macro transmission: dovish repricing lowers yields (bond prices up), weakens USD, supports gold
uncertainty_notes: The 700bp tradable threshold is far above the realistic 12h move for broad macro proxies from a single prediction-market shift; neither prediction is likely 'tradable' by that standard
Prediction-market probability for a full-year 2026 outcome is slow-moving and often reflects already-public Fed expectations rather than leaked information
Direction of any sharp move is unknown ex-ante; this card assumes a dovish (rising 6-cut probability) shift
A dovish move driven by recession fear could paradoxically send equities down while bonds/gold rally — macro signals are mixed

llm_justification.summary: This market measures expectations of an aggressively dovish 2026 Fed path (six 25bp cuts). A sharp rise in its implied probability signals lower expected rates, which maps most cleanly to higher long-duration Treasuries (TLT) and, secondarily, higher gold (GLD) via lower real yields and a softer dollar. However, this is a slow-moving, largely public macro expectation, the proxies respond modestly within 12h, and the realistic move is well below the 700bp tradable bar, so confidence is low-to-moderate and these are research observations, not signals.
key_assumptions: A sharp move in the market reflects a genuine dovish repricing, not thin-liquidity noise
Standard rate transmission holds: dovish path -> lower yields -> higher bond/gold prices
The prediction-market move contains information not already fully reflected in rates futures
failure_modes: The move was already public (driven by a known data release or Fed speak), so no edge exists
A dovish repricing from recession fear could be risk-off, muddying gold and pressuring equities instead
Thin prediction-market liquidity produces a probability move with no corresponding rates/FX follow-through — false signal
12h magnitudes for TLT/GLD are far below 700bp, so the mapping is directionally plausible but not tradable
llm_justification.why_not_ex_post: The card is timestamped, content-hashed, and never overwritten. Execution must reject any card created after an anomaly's trigger time.
